Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Short recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard from you
- Primary goal: move inference off the incumbent vendor to reduce unit costs while preserving latency and output quality for customer-facing recommendations.
- Priority tests: (1) OpenAI API compatibility for minimal SDK changes, (2) latency/cost baseline vs Bedrock, (3) prompt parity and tokenization differences that could affect outputs.

Redwood hypothesis / differentiators we discussed
- Redwood offers an OpenAI-compatible REST/SDK surface plus a model catalog. Customers typically swap SDK endpoints and run a small prompt-diff suite to validate parity.
- For throughput-sensitive paths we can map to a quantized variant and use prefix caching to hit latency SLOs without large cost increases.
- Smart routing allows fallbacks to hosted variants (faster) or dedicated (predictable) during the PoC.

Proposed PoC tests (high level) — attached is a detailed teardown (POC-test-plan.xlsx)
1) API compatibility: sample calls for completion, chat and function-like structured outputs; try a direct SDK swap to our OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
2) Tokenization and prompt diffs: run 50 canonical prompts (user->system->assistant) and compare outputs + token counts.
3) Latency & cost: 1k requests at 95th percentile measurement for both Bedrock and Redwood-hosted models using your production-like payloads.
4) Regression/quality: human or automated scoring for top-3 critical prompts.

Next steps / ask from FinLytics
- Share 30–50 representative prompts and a small sample of production request metadata (no PII).
- Confirm a 2-week window for the PoC starting March 16 (we think 10 business days of testing + 3 days for analysis).

I'll loop in Dev for the technical test scripts. Michael is on CC for any procurement/questions on dedicated options.

Availability for a 30-min kickoff: https://calendly.com/redwood/poc-kickoff-30

Thanks — I will stand up the PoC workspace and return a concrete test-run checklist by EOD tomorrow.

Alex / Priya — looping in a few technical notes and pragmatic caveats from the engineering side.

High-level: Redwood exposes an OpenAI-compatible API surface (same endpoints + similar JSON shapes). In practice the migration experience depends on four things: SDK usage patterns, streaming behavior, tokenizer differences, and model mapping. Below is an actionable checklist we use in PoCs.

Quick compatibility notes:
- SDK swap: In most cases swapping the base_url + API key and updating the client constructor is sufficient. We provide short snippets for Python/Node that mirror openai.ChatCompletion/Responses calls.
- Streaming: We support SSE streaming; payload framing is the same but read loops need minimal changes if your code expects different event delimiters.
- Function calling / structured output: We preserve name/type fields but recommend explicit schema validation on your side; small differences in null vs missing keys can occur for edge cases.
- Tokenization: Different model/tokenizer combinations change token counts and sometimes boundary splits. For prompts that depend on exact token offsets (e.g., regexes against raw tokenized strings), run our token-diff tool (included in prompt-diff-examples.md).

Proposed test scripts (we'll share via a repo):
1) token_count_check.py — runs your 40 prompts through both endpoints and outputs diffs (tokens, length, hashed output).
2) function_call_smoke.py — 200 calls to your invoice extraction prompt, validate shape, field names & types.
3) p95_latency_runner.js — parallel workers to approximate production concurrency and report p50/p95/p99.

Resource notes: For fair latency/cost comparison vs Bedrock: use identical concurrency and model-size families. If you can share expected concurrency peaks we’ll provision a matched Dedicated pool for the test or use hosted nodes with equivalent GPUs.

I attached a small markdown with examples where prompts produced different tokenizations (prompt-diff-examples.md). We recommend starting there to identify high-risk prompts.

Happy to run a 30-min tech kickoff during PoC week to walk through the scripts.

—Dev
